title: Asset and Border
premise: Marguerite Sandoval, a private security contractor who has spent twelve years guarding clients nobody trusts, is hired to protect a whistleblower whose voiceprint can unlock a server in Frankfurt holding evidence of a three-government surveillance cartel. When the voiceprint is stolen and used to trigger a kill order on Marguerite's own found family of contractors, they must smuggle the truth across borders, past an assassin who is a former lover, and through the loyalties of the team that raised them. In the end, Marguerite chooses truth over duty, burns their own cover to expose the cartel as the Frankfurt markets open, and survives—barely—to build a real family out of the wreckage.
about_author: Rosalind Galloway is a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for firms she cannot name, a career that ended when she realized the assessments were the product. She writes thrillers from a farmhouse in the Scottish Borders, where the nearest server is a neighbor's unreliable router.

chapters.title: The Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Marguerite Sandoval takes a routine protection contract on a nervous fintech auditor in Vienna, noting his paranoia exceeds his threat profile. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: professional detachment masking a low hum of unease that something in the file doesn't add up.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through a team briefing: how Marguerite joined Halcyon Detail, the private contractor that became their found family—gruff handler Okafor, tech prodigy Ines, ex-military twins. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: belonging built on shared secrets, and the first crack of doubt about whose secrets they are.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: The auditor reveals he carries a biometric key: the voiceprint of a dead EU regulator, capable of unlocking a server vault in Frankfurt. He begs Marguerite to listen to the recording. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: the moment curiosity curdles into complicity.

chapters.title: Kill Fee
chapters.summary: Ines discovers a contract on the auditor posted to a darknet broker—funded by a shell with fingerprints inside three governments. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into the cold clarity of a hacker who has found something too big.

chapters.title: The Vienna Extraction
chapters.summary: Assassins hit the hotel; Marguerite extracts the auditor through service tunnels, losing one of Halcyon's own in the crossfire. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: guilt and adrenaline fused—the rules just stopped working.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: Holed up in a Prague safehouse, the team debates handing the auditor over to their employer, Voss International. Okafor argues duty; Ines argues truth. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: a father-figure torn between the institution that made him and the people in front of him.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Portfolio
chapters.summary: We meet the assassin, Kestrel, reviewing photos of Halcyon Detail—and pausing on a twelve-year-old surveillance photo of Marguerite. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: professional calm over an old, unhealed wound.

chapters.title: What the Server Holds
chapters.summary: The auditor explains the Frankfurt vault: raw feeds from a joint surveillance program run by US, German, and British intelligence, sold to markets before it reaches parliaments. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: vertigo—the scale of what they're carrying.

chapters.title: Voss Calls
chapters.summary: Marguerite's employer orders them to deliver the auditor and the voiceprint to a Voss facility, no questions. Refusal means blacklisting—or worse. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: duty pulling one way, conscience the other.

chapters.title: Twins at the Door
chapters.summary: Kestrel's scouts probe the safehouse; the twins repel a silent entry attempt, but the team knows the quiet is over. POV: Tomas, the elder twin. Emotional beat: fear metabolized into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Dark
chapters.summary: Marguerite plays the regulator's recording alone at 3 a.m. and hears something impossible: a second voice on the tape—their own, from years ago, on a job they were told never happened. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: the floor of their identity gives way.

chapters.title: Ghost Job
chapters.summary: Marguerite confronts Okafor about the ghost job; he admits Halcyon was used as deniable labor for the cartel's earliest operations. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: shame of a handler who protected his people by lying to them.

chapters.title: Prague Burns
chapters.summary: Kestrel hits the safehouse with a drone strike; the team scatters, and the auditor is wounded. They split: Ines and the voiceprint west, Marguerite and the auditor south. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: found family fractured across a map, each piece carrying part of the truth.

chapters.title: Border Crossing, Nuremberg
chapters.summary: A checkpoint stop forces Marguerite to bluff past a border officer who has their real name on a watchlist. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: the terror of becoming visible after twelve years of engineered invisibility.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Terms
chapters.summary: Kestrel contacts Marguerite directly: hand over the voiceprint and Halcyon lives; refuse and the kill order extends to everyone. The voice on the line is achingly familiar. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: an assassin negotiating against their own heart.

chapters.title: The Person I Used to Be
chapters.summary: Flashback: Marguerite and Kestrel, lovers and colleagues a decade ago, separated when an operation went wrong and both were told the other had betrayed them. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: love remembered as both wound and compass.

chapters.title: Ines Offline
chapters.summary: Ines goes dark in Cologne after detecting a tracer on the voiceprint file; Marguerite must decide whether the mission or the person comes first. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: the thesis of the book stated in action—people over mission.

chapters.title: Cologne Cathedral Crowd
chapters.summary: Marguerite finds Ines alive but cornered in a train station crowd; they escape through a Christmas market as Kestrel watches from a balcony, rifle unfired. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: relief curdling into the knowledge that someone chose, deliberately, to miss.

chapters.title: The Broker's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ines decrypts a fragment of the broker's ledger: every Halcyon contract for twelve years was curated to build Marguerite's specific skill set. Someone raised them for this. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the found family revealed as also, possibly, a designed one—and choosing it anyway.

chapters.title: Voss's Face
chapters.summary: The team identifies the cartel's operational manager: Voss International's founder, Elena Brandt, who once signed Marguerite's first contract. POV: Brandt. Emotional beat: a villain's calm conviction that markets need certainty more than citizens need privacy.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Before Dawn
chapters.summary: The team converges on Frankfurt two days before the vault's quarterly purge, when the evidence will be permanently overwritten. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: a clock now ticking under every scene.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite approaches a Bundesnachrichtendienst contact who owes them; the contact warns that going official means all three services will bury them. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: the institutional door closes, and the only way through is the one they feared.

chapters.title: The Journalist's Price
chapters.summary: A Financial Times reporter agrees to run the story at market open—but demands the raw server data, not the voiceprint. They need the vault itself. POV: the reporter, Amara. Emotional beat: idealism negotiating with cynicism and finding common ground.

chapters.title: Kestrel Unmasked
chapters.summary: Marguerite ambushes Kestrel in a hotel bar; guns down, they finally speak. Kestrel reveals the ghost job was designed to burn them both, and that they've been hunting the cartel's ledger, not Halcyon. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: two people discovering their entire war was authored by someone else.

chapters.title: Uneasy Alliance
chapters.summary: Marguerite, Kestrel, and Ines plan a joint assault on the Frankfurt vault; Okafor, still loyal to Voss, is the unknown variable. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: trust rebuilt in the only currency assassins and spies share—competence.

chapters.title: Okafor's Choice
chapters.summary: Brandt orders Okafor to deliver his own team as proof of loyalty. He burns the order and sends Marguerite the vault's security rotations instead. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: an old soldier finally choosing his children over his flag.

chapters.title: The Vault Below
chapters.summary: The team enters the Frankfurt data center through a maintenance spine during shift change; the twins hold the door. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: brotherhood under fire, and the first real casualties of the endgame.

chapters.title: Voiceprint Verified
chapters.summary: At the vault terminal, the regulator's voiceprint unlocks the archive—but a duress alarm triggers, locking down the floor. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: triumph and trap arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: Brandt Arrives
chapters.summary: Brandt appears in the vault with private security, offering Marguerite partnership: the cartel survives on people like them, and always will. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: the villain's temptation made genuinely seductive—certainty, order, purpose.

chapters.title: The Betrayal That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Kestrel takes a bullet meant for Marguerite, revealing they'd secretly copied the archive to a dead-man's switch days earlier. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: love expressed as sacrifice, and a plan hidden even from allies.

chapters.title: Purge Protocol
chapters.summary: Brandt initiates the vault purge early; Ines races the deletion, carving out the core files while the twins hold the stairwell. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: a hacker's whole life compressed into a progress bar.

chapters.title: Markets Open
chapters.summary: At 9:00 a.m. Frankfurt time, Amara's story publishes with the archive mirror live; surveillance futures crater and three governments scramble to disown the program. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: the quiet, enormous moment when truth becomes fact in public.

chapters.title: The Long Corridor
chapters.summary: Marguerite confronts Brandt in the data center's spine corridor; Brandt nearly wins until Marguerite chooses arrest over execution, forcing the fight into daylight and cameras. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: the climax—duty to truth enacted as a refusal to become the monster.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Heartbeat
chapters.summary: Kestrel, critical in a Frankfurt hospital, is shielded from extradition by the scandal itself; Marguerite keeps vigil. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved—not chosen between, but fused.

chapters.title: Inquiries
chapters.summary: Parliamentary hearings begin; Okafor testifies, sacrificing his pension and reputation to bury Voss International for good. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: an old man's redemption, paid in full and without regret.

chapters.title: Halcyon, Dissolved
chapters.summary: The team formally disbands the company, each choosing a new name for themselves rather than a new employer. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: grief for an identity, gratitude for what it protected.

chapters.title: What Ines Kept
chapters.summary: Ines reveals she retained one encrypted copy of the archive—not to sell, but as insurance, and asks the team to vote on destroying it. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the found family's first fully honest decision, made together.

chapters.title: The Farmhouse Question
chapters.summary: Marguerite visits Kestrel recovering at a coastal safehouse; they discuss whether two people made by surveillance systems can ever be off the clock. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: tenderness with eyes open, love without illusions.

chapters.title: Asset and Border
chapters.summary: Marguerite burns their last cover identity, mails the final piece of evidence to Amara, and crosses no border at all—choosing to stay, visibly, in one place. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: the title resolved—an asset is something used; a border is something crossed; Marguerite refuses both.

chapters.title: After the Markets Close
chapters.summary: Months later: the team gathers at Okafor's cottage, unremarkable and unarmed, while news of Brandt's trial plays on a cheap radio. Marguerite steps outside and, for the first time, doesn't check the sightlines. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted—the found family surviving its own truth.
